land.text: Lower Nubia from the first cataract to the third; the Nobatae 'had been invited into the region from the Western Desert by the Roman Emperor Diocletian in 297 AD'

predecessors.note: Infobox 'Preceded by: Kingdom of Kush'. The kingdom 'only became tangible around 400 AD' (infobox 'Established: c. 400'); 347 is Cliopatria's hand-over from Kush. The northern valley (Kalabsha and the Dodekaschoinos) was Blemmyan until Silko.

land.text: the whole kingdom, 'annexed by their southern neighbor, Makuria'

successors.note: The merger 'most likely occurred before the Muslim conquest in 652' and 'By 707' at the latest; the Makuria page: 'likely during the 620s, before 642'. Nobatia continued as the eparchate of Nobatia under Makuria ('ruled by an eparch of Nobatia who was also titled the Domestikos of Pakhoras').

capitals.name: Pachoras (Faras)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Pachoras' ('Pakhoras' in the body, modern Faras). The page gives no coordinates; these are the researcher's for Faras on the west bank just north of Wadi Halfa, now under Lake Nubia (gazetteer name needed).

correction.text: the shape unchanged (147,534 km2, the first cataract to the third), ending in 641 rather than 646 because Makuria annexed Nobatia before 642; before Silko (c. 450) the northern valley from Philae to Kalabsha (Talmis), 'the capital of the Blemmyes', should be read as Blemmyan, which the ledger's 450 gain carries

keyframe_review.note: 347-646: the page dates the kingdom to c. 400 ('only became tangible around 400 AD') and Cliopatria to 347; kept from 347 with the found event at confidence 1. The southward extension 'incorporating the territory between the second and third Nile cataract' is undated and already inside the shape. Converted to Coptic Christianity in 543. No area figure in the infobox.

correction.text: not Nobatia: the land is Makuria's from 641 ('annexed ... likely during the 620s, before 642'; 'By 707, Nobatia had been annexed'); the shape is unchanged but its years go to the makuria dossier, whose makuria_623 keyframe adds it

keyframe_review.note: 647-655: Cliopatria keeps Nobatia to 655 and merges it in 656; the Second Battle of Dongola page has 'northern and central Nubia ... united under the Makurian king Qalidurut' in 652 and the Arabs fighting Makuria at Dongola in 642 and 652.

region.text: Lower Nubia between the first and third cataracts, settled by the Nobatae

ledger.note: 347: the Nobatae hold Lower Nubia after Kush. They 'had been invited into the region from the Western Desert by the Roman Emperor Diocletian in 297 AD'; the kingdom 'only became tangible around 400 AD' (infobox 'Established: c. 400'; first known king Silko c. 450). The year is Cliopatria's hand-over from Kush, not the page's.

region.text: the valley from Philae to Kalabsha (Talmis), 'the capital of the Blemmyes', after Silko 'claims to have driven the Blemmyes into the Eastern Desert'

ledger.note: c. 450: Silko drives the Blemmyes from the Nile. Infobox '450 A.D: Silko (first known king)'; the page does not date the war; the Blemmyes page: 'By the late 4th century they had occupied Lower Nubia and established a kingdom' with 'Kalabsha ... the capital of the Blemmyes' and cities at Faras, Ballana and Aniba, and lists Phonen c. 450. The region (the Dodekaschoinos, within 115 km of Aswan) is the researcher's; the blemmyes dossier (af-01-x) should carry the loss.

region.text: the whole kingdom from Philae to the third cataract

ledger.note: 641: Nobatia is absorbed by Makuria. 'The merger most likely occurred before the Muslim conquest in 652'; 'By 707, Nobatia had been annexed by their southern neighbor, Makuria'; the Makuria page: 'likely during the 620s, before 642' (a bishopric founded at Faras c. 630). 641 is the latest year consistent with 'before 642'; Cliopatria keeps the row to 655. Nobatia lived on as the eparchate of Nobatia within Makuria.

wars.name: Silko's war against the Blemmyes
wars.outcome: Silko, 'first known king' (infobox c. 450), 'claims to have driven the Blemmyes into the Eastern Desert'; Nobatia holds the Nile to Philae.
wars.note: Undated on both pages beyond the infobox's 450 for Silko and the Blemmyes page's Phonen c. 450; László Török 'doubted that one centralized Blemmyan kingdom ever existed'.

certainty.note: The northern frontier at Philae is Rome's treaty line from Diocletian's settlement of 297 and is sharp in effect; the southern frontier with Makuria (second or third cataract, Batn el-Hajar) and the desert edges are soft.

notes:
Dates. Cliopatria runs Nobatia 347-655; the page gives c. 400 for the kingdom and a merger into Makuria before 652 (Makuria page: 'likely during the 620s, before 642'; 'By 707' at the latest). This dossier keeps the 347 start (Cliopatria's hand-over from Kush, confidence 1) and ends in 641 so that the First (642) and Second (652) Battles of Dongola are fought by Makuria, as their pages have it; the makuria dossier's makuria_623 keyframe adds Nobatia from 641 and Cliopatria's nobatia_647 shape is marked wrong. A reviewer who prefers Cliopatria's 655 should move the merge in both dossiers together.

Blemmyes. The Blemmyes page has them holding Lower Nubia with a capital at Kalabsha from the late 4th century, with cities at Faras, Ballana and Aniba, which overlaps Cliopatria's Nobatia shape wholesale until Silko (c. 450). Only the northern valley (Philae to Kalabsha) is given to the Blemmyes here (ledger 450 at confidence 1), because the Nobatia page keeps Pachoras Nobatian and Török doubts a Blemmyan kingdom existed. The blemmyes dossier (af-01-x) should settle the 4th-5th-century split of Lower Nubia; the Kush dossier hands the Dodekaschoinos to the Blemmyes in 297 (Diocletian) on the same pages.

Gazetteer names needed: Faras/Pachoras (place, 22.2 N 31.48 E), Kalabsha/Talmis (place), Qasr Ibrim (place), Dodekaschoinos (region: Philae to Maharraqa), Batn el-Hajar (region: the second cataract reach). Pages silent: no area figure; no border point for the Makurian frontier; the Nobatia page does not mention the 641/642 Arab expedition.
